messages.subject: Factor with no latent effect
parts:
I'd like to have one of the factors in my IRT model based completely on a known predictor, with no latent part. Essentially, what I want to do is something like: 

mirt(df, covdata=covdata, 
                model=2, 
                formula=list(F1=~0 + KnownPredictor, F2=~1), itemtype = "2PL") 

This one seems to generate a fit.
I  then want to compare this to a model with only the known predictor

mirt(df, covdata=covdata, 
                model=1, 
                formula=list(F1=~0 + KnownPredictor), itemtype = "2PL") 


but this gives an error. 
Am I using the library incorrectly? Or is putting a 0 intercept in a latent regression not supported? 

Thanks.

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: Factor with no latent effect
parts:
I don't think such a thing is possible in the mirt() function right now, though you may be able to trick the mixedmirt() syntax into doing this. It would require specifying a latent regression model via lr.fixed, constrain the loadings to apply only to one latent trait, and set the residual variance of the trait to 0 (though not exactly 0, as this won't work in the computations of a density with the VCOV matrix). I'd have to experiment with this myself, though admittedly it is quite ad hoc. You might have better luck doing something like this in a SEM framework using a package like lavaan.

Phil
